Ref.No.OSEC11-022919 DILG Legal Opinion No. 14 s. 2012 ATTY. GEORGE A. ELIAS Vice Mayor CITY GOVERNMENT OF TAGUIG Dear Vice Mayor George A. Elias: This has reference to your letter duly indorsed by the Bureau of Local Government Finance (BLGF) thru its Executive Director, Ma. Presentacion R. Montesa. Your query arose from your allegations that "while the Honorable Mayor (of Taguig City) has issued the ARO for the release of the budgetary allotment for the salaries and wages of regular SP personnel, she had unceremoniously excluded the allocations for the SP casual, contractual and part-time employees and consultants despite the fact that there are budgetary allocations to this effect in the City's 2011 Annual Budget for personnel services of the Sangguniang Panlungsod. " In your letter, you inquired if in lieu of the Mayor, you can issue the subject ARO as regards the Sangguniang Panlungsod (SP) funds, applying the principle of "necessary implication" in order to enforce and carry out Sections 456 (I) and (2) of RA 7160 or the Local Government Code. While it is an alternative to refer your letter to the Commission on Audit (COA), which you might very well do under the circumstances, we shall nonetheless render an opinion on issues related to Section 456 of RA 7160 which you cited in your letter. On your allegations pertaining to the acts or omissions of the City Mayor, the Department shall defer rendering any opinion, comment or statement as they are not related in any way to your main query. While it is observed that the subject query pertains to issues affecting allocations in the City's 2011 Annual Budget which was passed and approved in 2010 and thus may appear mooted by the lapse of time, an opinion shall be nonetheless be rendered for academic purposes. Moving on to your query on whether the Vice Mayor can, by necessary implication, issue the ARO in relation to SP funds, we reply by quoting the definition of an Allotment Release Order per Commission on Audit Circular No. 96-002 dated 27 February 1996 entitled Accounting Guidelines and Procedures Relative to the Adoption of a Simplified Fund Release System in the Govemment which covers LGUs among others: "Allotment Release Order (ARO) is a formal document issued by DBM to the containing the authorization, conditions and amount of an agency allocation. The document may be a GARO or SARO. prior to the implementation of the SFRS, the document issued was the Advice Of Allotment (AA)". (emphasis and underscoring supplied). General Allotment Release Order (GARO) is a comprehensive authority issued to all agencies to incur obligations not exceeding an authorized amount during a specified period for the purposes indicated. It shall cover expenditures common to most, if not all, agencies without need of special clearance or approval from a competent authority. Special Allotment Release Order (SARO) is a specific authority issued to one or more identified agencies to incur obligations not exceeding a given arnount during a specified period for the purpose indicated. It shall cover expenditures the

release of which is subject to compliance with specific laws or regulations or are subject to separate approval or clearance by competent authority. By definition and as matter of strict policy by COA, the ARO is released to the head of the agency: and in case of LGUs, such head of agency is the local chief executive alone. Thus, to answer your query, the release of ARO to the Vice Mayor in lieu of the Mayor is not tenable. However, when funds are already within the coffers of the LGU for its appropriation and disposition, the local chief executive or the vice governor/ vice mayor is mandated to comply with the procedural requirements in the disposition thereof: Section 336. I-Ise of Appropriated Funds and Savings. - Funds shall be available exclusively for the specific purpose for which they have been appropriated. No ordinance shall be passed authorizing any transfer of appropriations from one item to another. However, the local chief executive or the presidinq officer of the sanqqunian concerned may, bv ordinance, be authorized to augment any item in the approved annual budget for their respective offices from savings in other items within the same expense class of their respective appropriations. Sec. 344. Certification on, and Approval of, Vouchers. — No money shall be disbursed unless the local budget officer certifies to the existence of appropriation that has been legally made for the purpose, the local accountant has obligated said appropriation, and the local treasurer certifies to the availability of funds for the purpose. Vouchers and payrolls shall be certified to and approved by the head of the department or office who has administrative control of the fund concemed, as to validity, propriety and legality of the claim involved. Except in cases of disbursements involving regularly recurring administrative expenses such as payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to govemment creditor agencies such as the GSIS, SSS, LBP, DBP, National Printing Office, Procurement Service of the DBM and others, approval of the disbursement voucher by the local chief executive himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed. In cases of special or trust funds, disbursements shall be approved by the administrator of the fund. In Case of temporary absence or incapacity of the department head or chief of omce, the officer next-in-rank shall automatically perform his function and he shall be fully responsible therefor. Further , Section 39 of the Manual on the New Government Accounting System for Local Government Units, prepared by the Commission on Audit (COA), is instructive (citing the case of Atienza vs Villarosa, G.R. 161081, 10 May 2005): Sec. 39. Approval of Disbursements. — Approval of disbursements by the Local Chief Executive (LCE) himself shall be required whenever local funds are disbursed, except for regularly recurring administrative expenses such as: payrolls for regular or permanent employees, expenses for light, water, telephone and telegraph services, remittances to govemment creditor agencies such as GSIS, BIR, PHILHEALTH, LBP, DBP, NPO, PS of the DBM and others, where the authority to approve may be delegated. Disbursement vouchers fer expen4itures appropriated for the operation of the Sanggunian shall be approved by. the. upvincipl Vice Govemor. the city Vice-Mayor or the municipal Vice-Mawr. as the case mav be. (emphasis and underscoring supplied) Again, the good Vice Mayor is not precluded from seeking the opinion of COA fo more definitive guidelines on ARO.
